Spectral wavelet decomposition enables localized frequency analysis, capturing transient dynamics missed by global Fourier methods. Multi-resolution analysis provides nested approximations that allow progressive refinement of signal features across scales. Time series entropy offers a scalar measure of complexity and unpredictability inherent in the data. These operators interplay: wavelets extract structure, MRAs provide hierarchical organization, and entropy evaluates information content. Failure modes include aliasing in wavelet transforms, loss of resolution in MRAs, and misinterpretation of entropy in non-stationary contexts. Dualities emerge between scale-space representations and information-theoretic measures, where increasing scale corresponds to decreasing entropy in smooth signals.
